podcast.body: Originally scheduled for mid-August 1995, its release was moved to August 14, 1995, to directly compete with Oasis's "Roll With It." In this "epic Britpop showdown," "Country House" sold 274,000 copies and secured the number one spot, winning the chart battle against Oasis. It entered the UK charts at number one and was certified triple platinum within a year, a "very nice, very proud achievement" despite Oasis winning the "overall war" of album sales. "It was called Country House."

podcast.body: This single, released on August 14, 1995, was a key component of the highly publicized "Record War" against Oasis's "Roll With It," a battle that garnered immense attention across Britain. "Country House" ultimately outsold its rival in the first week, moving 270,000 copies compared to Oasis's 220,000. This victory was partly attributed to a strategic move by Blur, who released two versions of the single, each containing different bonus tracks, thereby encouraging fans who desired all the songs to purchase both copies and significantly boosting its sales figures. "They sold more records in the first week, 270,000 copies to 220,000 for Oasis."
